outcome: Cephalometric variables (A point-nasion-B point angle (ANB), Wits values, sella-nasion-A point angle, sella-nasion-B point angle, Frankfort horizontal-mandibular plane angle, gonion-gnathion-SN plane angle)
cohort: The study included 90 age- and gender-matched patients who received treatment at Gaziantep University, Faculty of Dentistry Orthodontics Department, divided equally into normal and cesarean birth groups.
finding: The study suggests that the birth method may not significantly affect the development of the craniofacial skeletal system.
mod_finding: While ANB and Wits values were higher in the normal birth group, and sella-nasion-A point angle, sella-nasion-B point angle, Frankfort horizontal-mandibular plane angle, and gonion-gnathion-SN plane angle values were higher in the cesarean group, these differences were not statistically significant.
cross-section timing: Pretreatment (orthodontic) cephalometric radiographs were used, indicating measurements were taken when subjects sought orthodontic treatment, well after birth.
